reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Bitconnect by instructing viewers to join or register and invest $100 for 299 days in exchange for an almost $300 profit. The interface reinforces this solicitation with lending controls, guaranteed-interest language, a projected-earnings calculator, and an account display showing earnings. the available video evidence does not establish that the displayed terms or outcome were genuine or representative.

citations.quote: So I'm using the platform Bitconnect if you're new to it there is a link in the description where you can register for the site.
With Bitconnect you can just invest in the site
You're at least required to make $100 investment.
But once you have some bitcoin tokens in your wallet, you're going to click on Lend Bitconnect.

So, let's say you have $100 invested. It's a term of 299 days and you're going to get a profit of almost $300 and that's actually pretty good. So then you are going to click on i read the terms and then pay.

opening.argument: The presentation uses uncertainty rather than a formal promise: the speaker says “let's say” when describing a hypothetical $100 example and acknowledges he cannot perform the purchase at that moment. His personal result is presented as an experience, not proof that every viewer will receive the same outcome. The interface also requires the participant to read the terms before paying, which places the decision in the context of disclosed conditions rather than a hidden transfer. The available evidence therefore supports investment commentary based on one user's reported experience, but does not establish a guaranteed return or deception.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats a hypothetical example as a guarantee, but its quoted language begins with “let's say,” which signals an illustration. The cited instructions establish how the platform was presented, not that the terms were false or that the outcome was guaranteed. The opening also concedes that the evidence does not establish whether the displayed terms or outcome were genuine; that uncertainty cannot itself establish scam content.

citations.quote: So, let's say you have $100 invested. It's a term of 299 days and you're going to get a profit of almost $300
I don't know 7 USD. But once you have some bitcoin tokens in your wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The hypothetical framing does not neutralize the surrounding solicitation. The speaker expressly says viewers can register through the description and describes a $100 minimum, then tells them to lend for 299 days for almost $300. The terms screen shows lending amounts, accrued daily interest, and capital-release periods, while the calculator displays projected earnings. Calling these examples uncertain does not show that the advertised return is merely commentary.

citations.quote: there is a link in the description where you can register for the site
You're at least required to make $100 investment.
It's a term of 299 days and you're going to get a profit of almost $300

opening.argument: The video's observable structure is operational instruction: it walks a new user through receiving Bitcoin, opening the exchange, buying BCC, and navigating the lending menu. The speaker even states that he cannot complete one step because he lacks Bitcoin at that moment, which is consistent with a screen-based demonstration rather than a claim that viewers have already earned money. Explaining where controls are located and how a menu works is educational technology content. The dashboard, exchange, and lending screens show a platform workflow, but do not independently prove that the creator is certifying the service or guaranteeing its performance.

I can't do this right now because I don't have Bitcoin in my wallet right now
once you're on the page you're going to go to buy slash sell BCC

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's own quotations describe instructional steps, which supports a tutorial reading. Showing a registration link or explaining controls does not establish that the video makes a false factual claim. The account display and projected figures are interface content; the prosecution identifies no independent evidence that the creator altered them, that the platform could not operate as shown, or that every viewer was promised the same result.

citations.quote: the first thing you wanna do is go to receive bitcoin
then you are going to click on

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than neutral software instruction. The tutorial directs viewers to register, deposit Bitcoin, buy BCC, and lend it. It then supplies a concrete investment amount, term, and profit, and closes by directing viewers to the description. A demonstration can still be promotional scam content; the fact that the speaker explains interface mechanics does not show that the financial solicitation is educational rather than persuasive.

citations.quote: there is a link in the description where you can register for the site
Let's say you want to invest, I don't know, maybe $100 into the site.
So, let's say you have $100 invested. It's a term of 299 days and you're going to get a profit of almost $300
links in the description

opening.argument: The material can be understood as promotion of an external financial service and referral link, not proof of a scam mechanism. The description supplies a Bitconnect link, while the spoken walkthrough shows ordinary account operations: depositing Bitcoin, exchanging BCC, and selecting a lending amount. The supplied material does not show the creator requesting passwords or credentials, collecting deposits personally, promising downline income, or demonstrating that funds disappear. Even the speaker describes the displayed result as his own recent experience. Those limits matter: a risky or unsuccessful external service is not automatically established as deceptive from this record alone.

citations.quote: Join Bitconnect: http://www.bit.ly/cryptoyt
So I'm using the platform Bitconnect
So to look at my example, I just started out a few days ago with 160$ investment. And i've already earned more than 5$ in just 2 days.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies an investment flow, but an investment flow is not by itself evidence of a fraudulent mechanism. Its own opening says the available evidence does not establish whether the displayed terms or outcome were genuine or representative. The screen shows platform controls and an account history, yet no cited material establishes credential theft, a personal deposit destination, or downline compensation. The proper conclusion from those gaps is uncertainty about the service, not a proven scam classification.

citations.quote: I will start doing some give waste in the future, but I will be just for my referrals.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not credential theft or a personal wallet. The cited content directly promotes lending capital through Bitconnect: viewers are told to invest at least $100, use the lending function, and expect almost $300 after 299 days. The description's referral link and the closing reference to giveaways for referrals reinforce promotion. Missing evidence of every possible scam mechanism does not undermine the mechanism actually shown: soliciting funds into an investment program on stated return terms.
